reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: a member leaves a bucket of 50000 and joins another, membership in a Set (OIMBucketSlotsServiceSetDriven)
reading.floor: the same move, membership in a list kept in the caller's order (OIMBucketSlotsServiceArrayDriven)
reading.caveat: A BUCKET OF 50000, and the size is in the id because the answer is a function of it on BOTH halves. THE COUNT THIS PREDICTS, per member moved, through `bucketCollection.writeContent`: on the ordered half, `reconcile` compares the held list against the one handed in up to the swapped band, finds them unequal, drains all 50000 members and pushes all 50000 back, and the collection holds 50000 arrivals and unholds 50000 departures. On the unordered half: `reconcile` builds one Set of the 50000 slots handed in, probes it once per held member, deletes the one departure and adds the one arrival, and one hold is taken and one given back. The ordered half's sequence comparison stops at the swapped band, which is why the sweep over 16 positions (0, 3125, 6250, … 46875) exists: it averages that comparison length. ONE FLUSH IS SPREAD OVER 2 OPERATIONS, since a frame swaps one band in every lane at once; `flush.empty-vs-noop` prices a flush directly, for a reader who wants it out of the figure. WHAT AN OPERATION IS: one member moves from one bucket to another, through the only door the engine offers for it — two array stores that exchange the member between the two lists this file holds, `bucketCollection.writeContent` of each of those lists, a flush, and a read of every bucket in the frame through `getBucketMemberSlots`. Both halves run the identical body; the only difference in the process is which bucket service object the collection was constructed with. READINGS RECORDED BEFORE 2026-08-23 priced a re-file reached through a derived membership source and are not this operation. EVERY OPERATION REALLY MOVES A MEMBER, which is the failure this suite has already published a wrong number for: `writeContent` RETURNS without a wake when `reconcile` finds nothing arrived and nothing departed, and both halves would then time a frame in which no container was touched. Here the two lists handed in differ from what the buckets hold by exactly one member each, and `assertBandsAreWhereTheyAreExpected` checks each bucket holds exactly the members this file holds for it before the clock starts. The two rows of a swap are the two members of one band, one in each page of the lane, and the swap exchanges them — which is why this needs no `reset` at all: sizes, positions and the sweep are exactly what they were when the pass started, so an empty reset here is a steady state rather than a forgotten one. DIRECTION, three ways. (1) The two array stores, the mark, the flush and the read call are identical in SHAPE on both halves and inside both numbers, which pulls the RATIO toward 1.00, so the two printed nanosecond figures are the numbers to read. (2) ONLY THE SET HALF DIFFS: `OIMBucketSlotsServiceSetDriven.reconcile` takes the set difference (one Set of the list handed in, one probe per held member) and moves one hold each way, while the ordered half's `reconcile` compares the two sequences up to the first mismatch, then drains the whole list and re-adds every member, so every member it holds is unheld and held again. READINGS RECORDED BEFORE 2026-10-17 timed a set half that drained and refilled the whole set and an ordered half that kept a rank sorter and took a multiset difference, and are not this operation. (3) Both containers are walked every frame and stay in cache, which flatters both. A PASS IS WHOLE FRAMES, because half a swap would leave both members of a band in one page and every position after it would be a lie; so a pass may overshoot the operation count the prober asked for by fewer operations than there are pages, out of the tens of thousands it asks for.

reading.ours: for (const slot of bucketCollection.getBucketMemberSlots(bucket)) slot.entity — a Set of 10000, per member
reading.floor: the same walk of the same members, kept as a list, per member
reading.caveat: THE SENTENCE UNDER TEST is the one printed above the published removal table: "Both iterate at around [NO RUN BEHIND THIS FIGURE] 2 ns per element, and the difference between them is a fraction of that." It is the half of the bucket service argument that says the choice is NOT an iteration question, and it had no measurement behind it either. THE BODY IS THE SAME ON BOTH HALVES, character for character: one `getBucketMemberSlots`, one for-of, one field load and one store into the sink per member. The only difference in the process is what `getBucketMemberSlots` hands back — a `Set` on ours, the service's own array on the floor — so this row is a property of two JavaScript containers reached through one library, which is exactly what the sentence claims to be about. NOTHING IS WRITTEN, NO MEMBERSHIP IS SET AND NO FRAME IS CLOSED, and neither service orders anything on a read: the list hands back the array `priceGroupIndex` filled, in the order it was written. What a pass pays outside the walk is one service call and one iterator, spread over 10000 members. DIRECTION, three ways: (1) ours is measured on a set that was FILLED and never deleted from, so its entry table has no tombstones to walk — a bucket that has churned iterates worse, and this row therefore flatters the unordered half; (2) `slot.entity` is loaded per member on both halves, because a reader that visits members without looking at them is not a reader, and it is the same monomorphic field load on each side; (3) a pass is a whole walk of the bucket, so the operation count may overshoot what the prober asked for by fewer than 10000 members out of the millions a [NO RUN BEHIND THIS FIGURE] 25 ms pass visits.
